title: A third-party plugin's dependency hoists dsh-tools@0.0.1-rc.1 into the profile and the `tools` row is disabled, so the desktop host cannot boot

reported.symptom: after installing dsh-pdf@0.1.0 the desktop app never starts: `DesktopHostFatalError: dsh: startup failed: 1 required plugin did not activate`, with eight plugins waiting for the `tools` service (agent-loop, tool-working-directory, timeout-policy, spill-policy, session-checkpoint-policy, mcp-resources, cordis-host-runner, cordis-inspect-providers); disabling third-party plugins and reinstalling did not help
reported.runtime_trace: dsh: disabling profile plugin row "tools": Plugin @deepseek-ai/dsh-tools@0.0.1-rc.1 is incompatible with dsh 0.2.1-rc.2
user_hypotheses: the desktop installer is broken (no: the profile copy is the module the row resolves to)
reinstalling the desktop app fixes it (no: the hoisted copy is recreated with the plugin)
reported.root_cause: dsh-pdf@0.1.0 declares @deepseek-ai/dsh-tools ^0.0.1-rc.1 under dependencies, so pnpm places 0.0.1-rc.1 at <profile>/node_modules/@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools; profile-level names win over the installation copy, so the in-box `tools` row resolves to a three-generations-old manifest and is denied
reported.fix_verified_by_reporter: the thread's source-level reply: remove the copy's source (uninstall the plugin, prune the profile) or install it as a link whose package.json declares dsh-tools under peerDependencies; `dsh plugin allow-version` is explicitly the wrong remedy

deviations: the report does not print the requirement map; the key used here (@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent) is the first @deepseek-ai/dsh* peer of dsh-tools@0.0.1-rc.1 in stable key order, and all eight of its @deepseek-ai/dsh* peers are pinned to ^0.0.1-rc.1, so every one of them is unmet against 0.2.1-rc.2 — see plugin-dsh-tools.json (its ninth peer, @deepseek-ai/cordis, is not part of admission by project rule)
the `tools` row belongs to the in-box base bundle; it is re-mounted in the profile patch layer so the case stays a one-row reconstruction
bundles omitted: dsh-base / dsh-web-app are left out to keep the composition minimal
dsh-pdf@0.1.0 is materialised as the declaring manifest (its dependencies are what put the copy in place), but only the copy it hoists is what the verdict reads
the silent sibling shape the reply describes (a version-compatible old copy that instead splits TOOL_RUNTIME_SCHEDULER) is not modelled
